figurehead

/FIG-yer-hed/ - the stress falls on FIG · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Figurehead means a leader in title only, without real power.

Everyone photographs the parade marshal waving from the lead car, but the marshal is a figurehead; the parade office plans every float and street closure.

Example

The awards academy elects a celebrated actor as its president every two years, and every two years the actor learns the same lesson: the president is a figurehead who hands out envelopes, while the academy's paid staff choose the rules, the dates, and the budget.

Figurehead is exact where 'weak leader' is vague: a figurehead may be beloved, dignified, even useful at ceremonies — what defines the role is that the title carries no real power, because the power sits somewhere else.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

puppet: A puppet is a leader actively operated by someone hidden behind him: the strings are pulled, the lines are fed, the decisions arrive pre-made. A figurehead is emptier but freer — the title carries no power, yet no one is working him. A figurehead is left alone with an empty title; a puppet never is.

mouthpiece: A mouthpiece exists to deliver someone else's words aloud — a spokesperson reading the official line — and claims no leadership of his own. A figurehead holds a genuine title of leadership that simply commands nothing. A mouthpiece is defined by whose words he speaks; a figurehead, by the power his title lacks.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

kingpin: the person a whole operation actually turns on

commander: a leader whose orders are obeyed in fact, not just printed on the letterhead

Where it sits · how much real power the title holds

figurehead → deputy → autocrat

deputy vs. figurehead: A deputy already outranks a figurehead where it counts: the deputy's power is borrowed, but it is real, while the figurehead's grand title commands nothing.

autocrat vs. figurehead: The autocrat stands at the ladder's far end from the figurehead: every decision in the realm flows from the autocrat personally, while the figurehead decides nothing at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — figure: a shaped form or image

Root — head: the front or top

Put it together: Figure (a shaped form) + head (the front) = the figure at the front. On sailing ships the figurehead was the carved figure mounted at the bow — splendid, prominent, and steering nothing — and the word came ashore to name any leader who is all prow and no rudder.

Use the root in a new word: figurine: The shop's glass case of figurines is the first thing customers photograph when they walk in.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / political

Call a leader a figurehead when the title is real but the power is not: ceremonial monarchs, honorary presidents, chairmen kept for the letterhead. If someone behind the scenes actively works the leader like a marionette, puppet is the harsher, more accusing word; and the true holder of power — the potentate of this unit — is what the figurehead only appears to be.
